sources.title: AstroLife original editorial synthesis
sources.use: Original plain-language summaries and reflective prompts written for this knowledge base. Not a quotation or claim of empirical proof.
sources.rights_note: Original cards are CC BY 4.0. External sources are separately listed and retain their own rights.

sources.title: Astronomy Engine
sources.use: The current AstroLife calculation provider and its documented assumptions; not a claim of NASA/JPL equivalence.
sources.rights_note: MIT license in the upstream repository. Preserve its license and attribution when distributing code.

sources.title: Astronomy Engine — Kotlin API documentation, version 2.1.19
sources.use: Documents the exact coordinate functions used by AstroLife: geoVector returns a geocentric J2000 equatorial vector with light-time correction and optional aberration; equatorialToEcliptic converts it to true ecliptic of date (ECT); eclipticGeoMoon returns geocentric lunar ECT coordinates.
sources.rights_note: The library is included as a pinned dependency io.github.cosinekitty:astronomy:2.1.19. Retain the upstream MIT license. This source documents software methods and does not constitute a JPL ephemeris comparison.

sources.title: Astrodienst — Overview of chart types
sources.use: Used to distinguish natal, synastry, composite, multi-composite and natal-with-transits chart products and the underlying chart construction methods.
sources.rights_note: Taxonomy and method notes only; no copyrighted interpretation text is copied.

sources.title: Astro-Databank copyright and reuse policy
sources.use: Exclusion rule: no scraping or copying protected prose/images.
sources.rights_note: Astro-Databank explicitly prohibits spidering/scraping and reserves rights in its creative text and images.

sources.title: Cafe Astrology — Main categories
sources.use: Used to map learning and browsing categories: forecasts, tools, natal interpretations, free reports, synastry, basics, planets and points, predictive astrology, signs and horoscopes.
sources.rights_note: Taxonomy only; no article text or interpretations copied.

sources.title: Cafe Astrology — Free astrology reports and chart interpretations
sources.use: Used to structure readable report sections: placements, signs, houses, aspects, natal, transit and compatibility reports.
sources.rights_note: Taxonomy only; original explanatory prose is authored for AstroLife.

sources.title: A double-blind test of astrology
sources.use: A controlled test of claims about natal charts and personality matching.
sources.rights_note: Bibliographic citation and high-level summary only; no reproduction of article text.

sources.title: Appraisal of Shawn Carlson's Renowned Astrology Tests
sources.use: A published critique and reanalysis of the 1985 Carlson study; demonstrates that the debate should not be oversimplified.
sources.rights_note: Bibliographic citation and high-level summary only; no reproduction of article text.

sources.title: The relationship between date of birth and individual differences in personality and general intelligence: A large-scale study
sources.use: Large-sample analysis of more than 15,000 participants testing associations between birth-date/zodiac groupings and personality or intelligence; reported no support for the proposed zodiac effects.
sources.rights_note: Summarize the study design and its limits; no article text or protected tables are reproduced.

sources.title: The validity of astrological predictions on marriage and divorce: a longitudinal analysis of Swedish register data
sources.use: Longitudinal analysis of Swedish register data from 1968–2001; found no consistent evidence that astrologically favourable pairings were overrepresented in marriages or linked to lower divorce risk.
sources.rights_note: Use a short original summary with study population, period, outcome and limitations; do not reproduce article text.

sources.title: The Constellations
sources.use: Astronomical distinction between constellation boundaries, star patterns and cultural sky traditions.
sources.rights_note: Link and cite the source; do not copy its images or page text into this dataset.

sources.title: IAU Resolution B5 and Resolution 6A (2006)
sources.use: Official 2006 Solar System definitions of planet and dwarf planet and the classification of Pluto.
sources.rights_note: Cite the resolution. Do not describe Pluto as one of the eight IAU planets.

sources.title: The sun's position at birth is unrelated to subjective well-being: Debunking astrological claims
sources.use: Study of a nationally representative US sample (N=12,791) that reported no robust association between Western zodiac signs and eight well-being outcomes; effects accounted for 0.3% or less of variance.
sources.rights_note: Summarize the sample, measured outcomes and limitations without reproducing text or data tables.

sources.title: JPL Horizons API documentation
sources.use: Independent comparison fixtures for solar-system positions and explicit ephemeris settings.
sources.rights_note: Use documented API outputs and retain query settings, version, timestamp and attribution. Do not imply JPL endorsement.

sources.title: Horizons System User Manual
sources.publisher: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Solar System Dynamics
sources.use: Definitions and configuration for ephemerides, observing centres, coordinate frames, time scales, apparent coordinates, and uncertainty.
sources.rights_note: Use the manual as technical documentation. Record target, centre, time scale, reference frame, corrections, step size, and retrieval date for reproducible calculations.

sources.title: Planetary Physical Parameters
sources.publisher: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Solar System Dynamics
sources.use: Reference values for eight planets and five listed dwarf planets: radii, mass, density, sidereal rotation/orbital periods, V(1,0), geometric albedo, equatorial gravity and escape velocity. Only explicitly displayed uncertainties are stored.
sources.rights_note: Retain units, every displayed ± uncertainty, reference notes and retrieval date. A missing ± value means the JPL table did not supply one; it is not zero uncertainty. V(1,0) is defined at 1 au from both Sun and observer.

sources.title: Astrology and Science: A Critical Examination
sources.use: Review of empirical research on zodiac signs, Moon signs, ascendants and planetary aspects in relation to psychological variables; reports that most studies reviewed did not confirm astrological claims.
sources.rights_note: Bibliographic reference and brief original synthesis only.

sources.title: paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 model card
sources.use: Optional multilingual semantic-search experiment; not a mandatory runtime dependency.
sources.rights_note: Model card lists Apache-2.0 and 384-dimensional vectors across 50 languages. Review upstream dependencies before redistribution; do not bundle the large model in the default installer.

sources.title: Astronomy, Babylonia
sources.publisher: John Steele, Oxford Classical Dictionary / Oxford Research Encyclopedias (2021)
sources.use: Scholarly overview of Babylonian and Assyrian observation, mathematical astronomy, celestial divination and the historical overlap of astronomy and astrology.
sources.rights_note: Use bibliographic facts and original summaries only; full chapter access may be restricted.

sources.title: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos (Greek) — Ptolemaeus Arabus et Latinus
sources.publisher: Bayerische Akademie der Wissenschaften research project
sources.use: Scholarly catalogue of the Tetrabiblos, its four-book structure, and its Greek, Arabic and Latin transmission history.
sources.rights_note: Use the catalogue for history and manuscript/translation context. Do not treat historical doctrine as empirical proof or copy protected editions.

sources.title: Ptolemy's Tetrabiblos, translated by J. M. Ashmand
sources.use: Historical reference for classical astrological vocabulary and the history of traditional doctrine.
sources.rights_note: Project Gutenberg marks this edition public domain in the U.S. and asks readers elsewhere to check local law. This repository stores original summaries and a link, not the full translation.

sources.title: Swiss Ephemeris licensing information
sources.use: Exclusion rule until the project has selected and complied with a permitted license.
sources.rights_note: Dual AGPL/professional licensing. It is not included in this repository or bundled application by default.

sources.title: Synergy and Astrology — Persian astrology education and chart services taxonomy
sources.use: Used only to map Persian-facing service and content categories: natal chart, predictive astrology, horary, electional, medical astrology (excluded from health guidance), psychological astrology, Western, Vedic, Chinese and evolutionary traditions; zodiac-sign pages and educational content. No article text is reproduced.
sources.rights_note: Website is a secondary practitioner source, not an astronomy or clinical evidence authority. Category labels only; all original descriptions are newly written. Medical-astrology claims are excluded.

sources.title: Science versus the stars: a double-blind test of the validity of the NEO Five-Factor Inventory and computer-generated astrological natal charts
sources.use: A controlled test with 52 college students; participants identified their real NEO-FFI summaries above chance but could not identify their own computer-generated astrology summaries.
sources.rights_note: Bibliographic citation and high-level summary only; no reproduction of article text.

sources.title: Calendars ii. In the Islamic Period — the Jalali calendar
sources.use: Historical and calendrical reference for the Jalali reform, Nowruz at the vernal equinox, the first six 31-day months, the following five 30-day months, and leap-year handling. Use this to distinguish Solar Hijri month boundaries from fixed Gregorian dates.
sources.rights_note: Use bibliographic metadata and original concise summaries only; do not reproduce the encyclopaedia text.

sources.title: Nowruz iii. In the Iranian Calendar
sources.use: Reference for the modern Iranian calendar's Nowruz definition in relation to the vernal equinox and the first point of Aries, plus historical calendar reforms.
sources.rights_note: Use original summaries and cite the article; do not copy protected prose.

sources.title: A Concise Review of the Iranian Calendar
sources.use: Technical review of the Solar Hijri calendar, equinox-based year definition and intercalation. Use for calendar-method context, not as a statement that every month is identical to one tropical zodiac sign.
sources.rights_note: Link the paper and write original summaries; do not copy tables or text.

sources.title: Solar Return Chart — Astrodienst Astrowiki
sources.use: Used to distinguish a personal Solar Return chart (the exact time the transiting Sun returns to an individual's natal solar longitude, interpreted with the natal chart and a reference location) from a generic birth-month cohort horoscope.
sources.rights_note: Method taxonomy only; no copyrighted interpretations are copied.

sources.title: Transits of the Year — annual transit report structure
sources.use: Used only as a structural example: select a small number of significant, long-range transits, explain why they matter, and present opportunities and challenges in a readable 12-month narrative. The AstroLife cohort report is not the same as this personal natal-transit report.
sources.rights_note: Structure and taxonomy only; no authored interpretation text, images or paid report content is copied.

sources.title: Abu Ma'shar's Eight Treatises Regarding the Great Conjunctions, the Annual Revolutions, and Their Origins
sources.use: Bibliographic and historical record of Abu Ma'shar's work on annual revolutions of nativities and historical astrology. Useful for documenting the historical tradition, not validating predictive accuracy.
sources.rights_note: Use catalogue metadata and original historical summaries; inspect edition-specific rights before reproducing scans.

sources.title: The Jewel of Annual Astrology
sources.use: Scholarly study of annual astrology, annual revolutions and historical techniques for subdividing year-ahead readings. Use to understand historical method and terminology, not as empirical validation.
sources.rights_note: Full scholarly work may be copyright-protected. Store only a bibliographic link and newly written summaries.

sources.title: Mesopotamian astrology
sources.publisher: M. Willis Monroe, University of British Columbia / Wiley
sources.use: Scholarly overview of the emergence and institutional practice of celestial divination in the ancient Near East.
sources.rights_note: Original summary only; no protected article text reproduced.

sources.title: The Cuneiform Conception of Celestial Space and Time
sources.use: Context for Babylonian celestial terminology, astronomy, omen traditions and later transmission.
sources.rights_note: Bibliographic reference and original summary only.

sources.title: Ptolemy, Tetrabiblos (Loeb Classical Library translation)
sources.publisher: Harvard University Press / Loeb Classical Library
sources.use: Historical source for Hellenistic astrology; Book I distinguishes astronomical calculation from less certain astrological inference, while Books II–IV cover general and individual topics.
sources.rights_note: Do not reproduce protected translation; original summaries and bibliographic references only.

sources.title: Abū Maʿšar (Albumasar)
sources.publisher: Encyclopaedia Iranica, article by David Pingree
sources.use: Biographical and transmission context for Abū Maʿšar and the Greek, Indian, Sasanian, Syrian and Arabic sources he synthesized.
sources.rights_note: Original summary only.

sources.title: Astrological Treatises, MS M.785
sources.use: Evidence for the illustrated Latin abridgement of Abū Maʿšar and the medieval manuscript tradition; the catalogue notes the linguistic transmission question.
sources.rights_note: Catalogue metadata only; manuscript images remain subject to the holding institution's terms.

sources.title: Al-Tafhīm li-Awāʾil Ṣināʿat al-Tanjīm
sources.use: Documents al-Bīrūnī's Persian and Arabic instructional work in question-and-answer form for learners of mathematics and astrology.
sources.rights_note: Original summary and catalogue facts only.

sources.title: Kitāb al-tafhīm (Persian and Arabic manuscript records)
sources.publisher: Institute for the History of Science / Max Planck Society, ISMI
sources.use: Language and bibliographic metadata for the Persian and Arabic versions of al-Bīrūnī's text.
sources.rights_note: Metadata and original summary only.

sources.title: Toward a History of Hebrew Astrological Literature
sources.publisher: Reimund Leicht, Cambridge University Press, Science in Medieval Jewish Cultures
sources.use: Bibliographic survey of medieval Jewish astrological writing and the differing positions of Jewish intellectual authorities.
sources.rights_note: Original summary only; no chapter text reproduced.

sources.title: Astronomy and Astrology in the Works of Abraham ibn Ezra
sources.publisher: Bernard R. Goldstein, Cambridge University Press
sources.use: Context for Ibn Ezra's Hebrew scientific works and the transmission of Arabic astronomy and astrology into Latin and Hebrew scholarship.
sources.rights_note: Original summary only.

sources.title: Jyotiṣa Sanskrit text collection
sources.use: Index to Sanskrit text witnesses and public digital editions including Bṛhajjātaka and other Jyotiṣa works; individual editions require provenance checks.
sources.rights_note: Check rights and edition notes for each linked text; do not assume all scans or translations share one licence.

sources.title: The Bṛihat Saṃhitā of Varāhamihira (1884–1885 translation)
sources.use: Digitized historical English translation and bibliographic record for Varāhamihira's encyclopaedic Sanskrit work.
sources.rights_note: Wellcome lists the item as Public Domain Mark; verify the status of any separately reused scan or derivative.

sources.title: The Dresden Maya Codex: content and astronomical tables
sources.publisher: Saxon State and University Library Dresden (SLUB)
sources.use: Catalogue and scholarly institutional explanation of the Dresden Codex Venus and eclipse tables.
sources.rights_note: Original summary; manuscript images are not copied.

sources.title: The Dresden Codex
sources.use: Bibliographic description of the codex, its 39 leaves, Venus calculations, eclipse material and ritual calendars.
sources.rights_note: Catalogue metadata and original summary only.

sources.title: Astronomy in the Maya Codices
sources.publisher: Harvey M. Bricker and Victoria R. Bricker, Smithsonian Institution
sources.use: Scholarly reference on Maya calendrical cycles, Venus, eclipses, planetary and seasonal astronomy in the codices.
sources.rights_note: Bibliographic reference and original summary only.

sources.title: The design and reconstructible history of the Mayan eclipse table of the Dresden Codex
sources.publisher: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences / PubMed Central
sources.use: Research on the 405-lunation structure and historical reconstruction of the Dresden Codex eclipse table; this concerns eclipse prediction, not a Western natal zodiac.
sources.rights_note: Original summary only; check final publication metadata and version before citing in a formal edition.

sources.title: CHANI — 2026 Sign-by-sign Horoscopes
sources.use: Reference for sign-by-sign annual horoscope navigation and the distinction between Sun-sign and rising-sign readings. Used for structure only.
sources.rights_note: No prose, illustrations or interpretations are copied. AstroLife cards contain original editorial synthesis.

sources.title: CHANI — How to work with astrology on a daily basis
sources.use: Reference for explaining transits through houses and life areas, distinguishing short and long transit durations, and following longer storylines through time.
sources.rights_note: Method and taxonomy reference only; no protected wording or app content is reused.

sources.title: Cafe Astrology — Monthly Horoscopes
sources.use: Reference for sign-by-sign forecast organisation and separating romance, career and general-life themes. Used to benchmark structure and readability.
sources.rights_note: No article text, illustrations or interpretations are copied; all AstroLife prose is original.

sources.title: Cafe Astrology — 2026 Planetary Overview
sources.use: Reference for the chronology of planetary ingresses, retrogrades and year-level event timelines. AstroLife uses its own calculated ephemeris and does not copy the site's dates or interpretations.
sources.rights_note: Calendar structure only; no proprietary interpretations or images are reused.

sources.title: Cafe Astrology — This Month in Astrology
sources.use: Reference for pairing a short narrative overview with a chronological planetary-event timeline and sign-by-sign summaries.
sources.rights_note: Editorial structure only; all AstroLife content is independently authored.
